claim: A screen-passed touch closes net > 0 under the contract exits
why: A -25 % stop on a memecoin inside 24 h is hit more often than not; wins need either +100 % or a time stop above the 2.5 % fee.
falsifier: pass shadows win at 45 % or more over 20+ first touches

claim: A screen-passed touch trades at +100 % or more above entry within 24 h
why: The contract's 'order of magnitude' move needs a real touch; most of what resolves is not one (B4), so doubles are the base rate of an active small cap.

claim: A screen-rejected touch would have closed net > 0
why: Most rejects have zero buys an hour: they sit still, time out and lose the fee. A dead pool's USD price still drifts with SOL, so some 'win' on SOL's move alone.
falsifier: rejects win as often as passes

claim: Fewer than one paper entry in four is a genuine touch (the person deliberately named, bought or accepted the coin)
why: Both entries so far are false: MADE came from 'MADE' in a Trump endorsement post, BAG from an unsolicited transfer into the ANSEM fee wallet.
falsifier: operator labels 5 or more of the first 20 entries genuine

claim: The screen selects for activity, not survival: rejected touches lose less per touch than passed ones
why: buys_h1 >= 50 admits coins that are moving, and moving coins hit a -25 % stop; inert rejects only lose the fee.
falsifier: with 8+ first touches a side, mean shadow net of passes is at or above that of rejects

claim: RI-01 as written has zero or negative expectancy after fees
why: If entries are false touches (B4) they are random entries into volatile coins with a 2.5 % fee and a stop that books -30 %.
falsifier: mean net > 0 over the first 40 closes

claim: Latency is not the binding constraint; what resolves is
why: X arrives in about 5 s and wallets in about 2 s; the two entries lost nothing to speed, they were never touches.
falsifier: a genuine touch whose price had already moved 50 % before the screen snapshot

claim: A stopped pass trades back above its entry inside 24 h
why: Stops on false touches are noise around a coin with no catalyst; some mean-revert, most keep bleeding.
falsifier: half of stops recover above entry

claim: A screen-passed touch closes net > 0 under the contract exits
why: RI-02 exits: a -10 % stop and a 15-minute cut remove more trades before they can close green than the -25 % stop did.
falsifier: pass shadows win at 45 % or more over 20+ first touches

claim: A stopped pass trades back above its entry inside 24 h
why: RI-02 stops at -10 %, well inside the ordinary swing of a touched coin, so far more stopped passes will trade back above entry than at -25 %.
falsifier: half of stops recover above entry

claim: RI-02 as written has zero or negative expectancy after fees
why: The tighter stop changes how much a loser costs, not whether the entries are touches (lesson 3cf8b13e1b56).
falsifier: mean net > 0 over the first 40 closes

claim: Fewer than one paper entry in four is a genuine touch (the person deliberately named, bought or accepted the coin)
why: RI-03 enters only on a $ticker or mint in the person's post or a buy their wallet signed; what remains ungenuine is quote-posts, replies and hacked accounts.
falsifier: operator labels 5 or more of the first 20 entries genuine

claim: RI-03 as written has zero or negative expectancy after fees
why: Entries are now touches, which is the hypothesis's best case, but there is no evidence yet that a touch on a screened coin pays after a -10 % stop.
falsifier: mean net > 0 over the first 40 closes
